tests/MyRestaurant.EndToEnd.Tests/Harness/HandheldReach.cs — two new HandheldSurface records, KitchenPass and KitchenRecall, both anchored on #kitchen-board-surface[data-live='true'][data-loaded='true'], with every selector required for both reach and the 16px font floor (F-127's lesson applied on the way in, not a slice later).

tests/MyRestaurant.EndToEnd.Tests/EndToEndScenarios.cs — §16.3 scenario 6 renamed to Kitchen_FulfillsLineFromAHandheld_GuestSeesFulfilledBadge and rearranged: a kitchen credential is created, signed in by password on a 375×667 isolated context, the forced change completed, and the board opened before the guest sends — so the KitchenAlert arrives while the board is live and the badge exists to be measured. Two measurements, both MeasureHereAsync because navigating would destroy the alert state: the pass while work is waiting, and the board once a line is away and the undo exists. The fulfilment moves from the administrator's wide page to the handset; the wide board becomes the observer. AssertHandheldBarrier's viewport message was made surface-neutral (Slice 73 wrote it counter-specific).

Reasoned height/font/reach check against app.css (not executed): every measured control resolves to ≥44px via --touch-target or .kitchen-line-button's min-height: 3rem, and every one inherits 1.05rem from .kitchen-board or declares 1.1rem, so the 16px floor clears. At 375px the panel's content box is 313px and the widest flex row (.kitchen-menu-item) sums to ~279px at its declared bases.

Session ritual
Reconstructed all 390 files from dump.txt with per-file SHA-256: 389 verified, LICENSE elided by design. Drift found and reported: Slice 73 had landed, contrary to session memory.

Gates emulated against the delivered tree: version header ↔ newest changelog entry (v1.59 / 2026-08-30, history descending), Markdown table integrity, §16.4 counted-class census, byte hygiene, no comments in authored C#, withheld-document links intact. The two table-gate flags my emulator raises fire identically on the pristine tree — pre-existing artifacts of my escaped-pipe handling, not regressions.

What landed
The kitchen is worked from a handset for the first time. A kitchen account is created, signed in by password on an isolated 375×667 context, forced-change completed, and the board opened before the guest sends — because KitchenAlertState is a field on the circuit, and a board opened after the send has an unseen count of zero, so .kitchen-alert-badge wouldn't exist to measure. The line is then fulfilled from the handset while the administrator's wide board observes; the write and the read are now on two contexts held by two people.

Two measurements: the pass while the alert stands (appending acknowledges it), and the board once a line is away (Undo exists only inside the fulfilment window). Both where they stand — a navigation resets the circuit fields being measured. Every selector required for reach and text, which is F-127's lesson applied on the way in.

F-129. Slice 73 wrote it names four into §11.12 and closed the same paragraph with which is why the set is written down and not counted — one slice before the slice that makes it six. The count is deleted rather than corrected (F-77, F-89); what replaces it is what a list can't carry: what's outside the set and why. The kitchen's deferral sentence goes rather than being softened, because its subject has ceased to exist (F-41).

Stage 1 closes — the last row the plan opened on 2026-08-11.

What was not verified
Nothing compiled — no SDK, so 1332 is arithmetic. No browser ran; neither measurement has matched an element. The thinnest claim in the slice: that the kitchen board fits inside 375px is read out of app.css — a 313px panel content box against a widest declared row of roughly 279px. That margin is narrow enough that a real run is the only thing that settles it, and if anything fails here, that's where to look first. Three veto points with reversion instructions are in _CHANGES.md.
